questions.stem: What common goal do Data Perturbation, Data Swapping, Data Shuffling, Data Scrambling and Data Obfuscation share?
options: Reducing the size of a dataset
Hiding the identity of an entity while keeping the essence of the data
Converting data into a new file format
Making data reversible at any time
Summarising data into ranges
questions.explanation: All of these use the same technique to hide the identity of an entity but keep the essence of the data.

options: Removing identifiable values from a dataset
Summarising identifiable values into ranges
Encrypting values with a shared key
Replacing the values of data at the same level of detail as the original data
Moving data from one server to another
questions.explanation: Data Swapping replaces values at the same level of detail as the original, so the cardinality of the replaced data is maintained.

questions.stem: What property of the data is maintained when values are replaced by Data Swapping?
options: Cardinality
Encryption
File size
Column names
Row order
questions.explanation: In Data Swapping the cardinality of the replaced data is maintained because values are replaced at the same level of detail.

questions.stem: How do Data Anonymisation, Data Generalisation and Data Swapping each treat identifiable data?
options: All three remove it
All three summarise it
Anonymisation summarises it, Generalisation removes it, Swapping encrypts it
Anonymisation replaces it, Generalisation removes it, Swapping summarises it
Anonymisation removes it, Generalisation summarises it, Swapping replaces it at the same level
questions.explanation: In Data Anonymisation identifiable data is removed, in Data Generalisation it is summarised, and in Data Swapping the level of identifiable data is replaced.

questions.stem: Who mainly uses the Data Swapping technique?
options: Marketing teams preparing campaigns
Auditors reviewing compliance
Data Scientists and Data Citizens who need data at the lowest level to create and train Machine Learning models
Network administrators
Legal teams drafting contracts
questions.explanation: Data Swapping is mainly used by Data Scientists or Data Citizens who require data at the lowest level to create and train their ML models.

questions.stem: In the age example of Data Swapping, with which value is the age 26 swapped?
questions.explanation: To keep the same level of detail, ages are swapped such as 26 with 59, 28 with 58 and so on.

options: Swapping that replaces every value in the column
Swapping that summarises values into ranges
Swapping that removes half of the records
Swapping that is fully reversible
Swapping that does not replace all the values
questions.explanation: Partial Swapping does not replace all the values, whereas Full Swapping replaces all of them.

questions.stem: How reversible are Data Perturbation, Swapping, Shuffling, Scrambling, Obfuscation and Masking?
options: They are a permanent change of data, very hard to revert and in most cases not reversible
They are always reversible with the original key
They are reversible only for structured data
They are reversible within 24 hours
They never change the stored data
questions.explanation: All of these techniques are a permanent change of data and are very hard to revert; in most cases they are not reversible.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named as part of the same family of identity-hiding techniques as Data Swapping?
options: Data Shuffling
Data Scrambling
Data Encryption
Data Obfuscation
Data Perturbation
questions.explanation: The family comprises Perturbation, Swapping, Shuffling, Scrambling, Obfuscation and Masking; encryption is not listed among them.

questions.stem: In Data Swapping, what does NOT happen to the data being protected?
options: Its values are exchanged with other values
Its level of detail is preserved
Its cardinality is maintained
It is removed or summarised into another column
It becomes usable for training Machine Learning models
questions.explanation: With Data Swapping the data is not changed at modelling normalisation level, not removed and not summarised in another column; the values are simply swapped.
